messages.subject: missing data & lavaan
parts:
Hello,
I am running a dataset with incomplete data (MAR). The data are ordinal, so I am interested in using WLSMVS or ULSMVS.

When I run these methods with 'missing=default'  and  'missing = pairwise', I get different results.  (Not greatly different, but still - different).
This leads me to the following questions:
-What is the difference in the options default & pairwise for these estimators?

-From my understanding, the pairwise option is similar to FIML (just with WLSMVS -using an ordinal estimator)--this is also similar to Mplus, correct?

Thanks for any assistance,
Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: missing data & lavaan
parts:
When I run these methods with 'missing=default'  and  'missing = pairwise', I get different results.  (Not greatly different, but still - different).
This leads me to the following questions:
-What is the difference in the options default & pairwise for these estimators?
I think the default is listwise deletion, whether data are categorical or continuous.  You can verify this by comparing the sample sizes using the two methods.
-From my understanding, the pairwise option is similar to FIML (just with WLSMVS -using an ordinal estimator)--this is also similar to Mplus, correct?

Only in the sense that no rows of data are thrown away as long as they are observed on at least one (FIML) or two (WLS) variables.

Terry
